Aidan Hogan

I'm Aidan. This is my academic homepage.

I'm a Professor in the Department of Computer Science (DCC) at the Universidad de Chile, and an Associate Researcher of the Millennium Institute for Foundational Research on Data (IMFD).

I previously worked at the Digital Enterprise Research Institute (DERI) (now called INSIGHT) based in the National University of Ireland, Galway. I started there in April 2005, doing an internship and various other things, including a PhD which I defended in February 2011. Then I did a PostDoc for two years or so. I left DERI/INSIGHT for Chile in November 2013.

My general research interest is in exploring whether or not the Semantic Web and Linked Data are good proposals for organising the content of the Web.

My main research goal is to one day write a good paper.

Errata

Mistakes happen. This is a list of some errata found in the published versions of the works listed above (works with errata have been marked above with the following symbol: ). The errata listed have been corrected in the pre-print versions linked above.

  • In the published version of "The Ring: Worst-Case Optimal Joins in Graph Databases using (Almost) No Extra Space", Theorem 7.9 holds only for cycles, not for general order graphs (see details). We thank Ruben Becker, Adrián Gómez-Brandón, Gonzalo Navarro and Nicola Prezza for this correction!
  • In the published version of "Semantics and Canonicalisation of SPARQL 1.1", Table 7, in the definition for projection, it should read "dom(μ) = V ∩ dom(μ′)" instead of "dom(μ′) = V ∩ dom(μ)". We thank Median Hilal for the correction! This is corrected in the version linked above.
  • In the published version of "Modelling Dynamics in Semantic Web Knowledge Graphs with Formal Concept Analysis", we stated Mean Average Error (MAE), when we intended to say Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Also on line 20 of Algorithm 1, B_i should rather be B_j'. This is corrected in the version linked above.
  • In the published version of "Fast Approximate Autocompletion for SPARQL Query Builders", we claimed that "In terms of experiments, to the best of our knowledge there is no existing benchmark for autocompletion." This was erroneous: in "Efficient SPARQL Autocompletion via SPARQL", Bast et al. (also cited in the paper) define a benchmark for autocompletion with respect to Wikidata, Freebase and Fbeasy.
  • In a pre-print version of "Canonical Forms for Isomorphic and Equivalent RDF Graphs: Algorithms for Leaning and Labelling Blank Nodes", Definition 3.18 forgot to specify that G' be a subset of G. Thanks to Antoine Zimmermann for pointing out this issue, along with some other minor comments! (I'm hoping to correct for the published version.) In the published version, on P24, second paragraph, as well as in Example 4.15: [_:a,_:c] should read [_:a,_:b]; [_:c,_:a] should read [_:c,_:b]; [_:c,_:i] should read [_:c,_:f]; and [_:a,_:g] should read [_:a,_:d]. Also in Algorithm 3, the recursion of the distinguish function requires making a copy of the array. Thanks to Ivan Herman for these latter corrections! Manu Sporny has pointed out that his joint (and earlier) work with Dave Longley on producing canonical labels for blank nodes was not cited in this paper; we have added this missing reference and given due credit to this earlier work. Also, on line 26 of Algorithm 6, G' should be G, the case where the join returns empty results for an intermediate solution has now been clarifed by adding lines 44–45, the condition on line 28 was fixed to assure termination, and other clarifications were added (thanks to Dan Kortschak). Finally, in the discussion after Definition 4.6, it was implied that the split of G in Example 4.5 would be G, whereas G should be split into two subgraphs (credit to Tomás Vallejos for spotting this). These issues are resolved in the version linked above.
  • In the published version of "Reifying RDF: What Works Well With Wikidata?", in Table 5 and Figure 3, the standard reification and n-ary relations columns were mixed up; also, the minimum y-value (100 ms) used for Figure 3 was higher than the runtime of two query executions for Virtuoso (Q7: NR & SP), which thus did not appear in the figure. These errors are fixed in the version above.
  • In the published version of "Everything you always wanted to know about blank nodes", there was a bug with how SPARQL SELECT queries were used to find non-lean graphs: we neglected to address automorphisms that would cause graphs to appear non-lean when they were actually lean. The discussion at the end of Section 4.2 and Algorithm 5 have been updated accordingly to fix the issue in the version linked here. (Here's some more details on the error I sent to my co-authors.) Also, in Theorem 3.5, it was stated that G entails H if and only if I(H) is contained in I(G); this should have stated if and only if I(G) is contained in I(H). Finally we removed a duplicate node in Figure 1 (thanks to Georg Lausen). These errors are fixed in the pre-print above.
  • In the published version of the Hogan book chapter in Linked Data Management, in the first definition, I had stated "U ∩ B ∩ Lp ∩ Lt = ∅" to indicate that the sets were pair-wise disjoint; however, this does not ensure that the sets are pair-wise disjoint, just that there is no element of all four sets. The erroneous notation has been removed from the pre-print linked above. (Thanks to Basil Ell for pointing this out!)
  • In the published version of the Buil-Aranda et al. paper at ISWC 2013, the percentage of endpoints falling into the availability intervals discussed in Section 5.2 did not add up to 100% but rather to 97%. Most notably, in the 95–99% interval, the percentage should be 17.4%, not 14.4%. This has been corrected in the pre-print linked above. (Thanks to Ruben Verborgh for pointing this out!)

If you found another error in one of the works listed above, please get in contact so I can list it here. It would be much appreciated!
